evidence.text: '''Abyssal demons''' are one of the [[strongest]] types of [[demons]], requiring level 85 [[Slayer]] to be damaged. Alongside their [[Abyssal Sire|boss variant]], they are the only creatures in the game to drop the [[abyssal whip]] and [[abyssal dagger]]. They have relatively high accuracy but their max hit of 8 is low for their combat level.

In combat, abyssal demons are capable of teleporting either themselves or the player around, meaning that [[safespotting]] is not viable. When landing a [[successful hit]] on an abyssal demon, it has a 1/6 chance to teleport away, followed by a 1/3 chance to teleport the player away in case the first roll fails.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1307639253657157632|date=20 September 2020|archiveurl=https://reldo.runescape.wiki/i/98425|archivedate=28 February 2023|quote=When they're executing the damage code (even with a damage value of 0) they call a 1/6 chance of teleporting themselves, and if that fails they call a 1/3 chance of teleporting the player. Magical splashing doesn't execute damage code (i.e. no hitsplat) hence what you observe.}} Abyssal demons can teleport players up to 20 tiles away.{{CiteTwitter|author=Mod Ash|url=https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1489689419636477954|date=4 February 2022|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220204200200/https://twitter.com/JagexAsh/status/1489689419636477954|archivedate=4 February 2022|quote=The max range of their teleport is 20 tiles, so being teleported 20 tiles is conceivable. (...)}} When teleported, you will stop attacking the demon. Having [[Auto Retaliate]] turned on can help make sure you fight back. The forced teleport on the player can be avoided by reading a [[Teleport anchoring scroll]].

includedStates: Three215 spawn definitions explicitly one per combat style,all max7. Parent Nechryarch and normal deathspawn2 are separate actors; despawning ends attacks without causing a terminal hit.

evidence.text: These chaotic spawns are more accurate than their normal variants and have a higher max hit of 7. However unlike their normal variants, their attacks can be blocked with [[protection prayers]], however they are spawned each using a different combat style. The best way to deal with the chaotic spawns in single-way areas is to run away until they lose interest, as they will not target the player again when they attack the nechryarch, though they may be summoned again. In multi-way areas, they can be killed with burst/barrage spells instead.

Rather than being summoned one at a time like normal death spawns, the nechryarch summons 3 chaotic spawns immediately when it calls for them. The chaotic spawns also cover all three forms of the combat triangle; one uses melee, another uses magic, and the other one uses range.

evidence.text: While assigned a bloodveld Slayer task, players with the [[Slayer Rewards|Bigger and Badder]] perk unlocked have a 1 in 200 chance for an [[Insatiable Bloodveld|insatiable bloodveld]] to appear after each kill. However, bloodvelds in the [[God Wars Dungeon]] and [[Wilderness God Wars Dungeon]] do not spawn superiors.
As [[demon (attribute)|demons]], bloodvelds are susceptible to [[demonbane weapons|demonbane weaponry]].

In the [[Slayer Tower]], bloodvelds can be [[safespotted]] in the centre room either in the north-eastern corner behind the chair or next to the armour stands and wardrobes around the walls. On the task-only basement floor, a safespot exists in the north-west corner between the chest, chair, broken table, and shelves. Bringing [[nature rune]]s for [[alchemy spells]] is recommended, as bloodvelds frequently drop [[fire rune]]s and items with good high alchemy value. An additional safespot is found in the corner between the torch and the armour set.

In the [[Stronghold Slayer Cave]], bloodvelds can be safespotted while using a [[dwarf multicannon]] in the north-east section of their area, though this spot is often crowded. An additional safespot in the Stronghold Slayer Cave is located in the east room, north of some rocks and east of a pillar.

In the [[God Wars Dungeon]], bloodvelds can be safespotted behind piles of bricks directly north-east of the exit rope, though a player should equip both a [[Saradomin item|Saradomin]] and [[Zamorak item]] when using this safespot. Another option exists further to the north-east, behind the rock formations on the coast. Once inside, this spot requires only a Zamorak item.
In the [[Wilderness God Wars Dungeon]], with both a [[Saradomin item|Saradomin]] and [[Zamorak item]] equipped, rocks can be used to safespot bloodvelds.

evidence.text: Sarachnis attacks with [[melee]] when players are adjacent to her, and [[ranged]] when they are out of melee range; she also heals upon dealing damage. Her attacks are accurate and can hit up to 31, so it is important to pray against her attacks correctly. Every four attacks, she will bind the player with a web that deals no damage but prevents them from moving for a few seconds, and will then move somewhere else in the arena. The web's duration can be fully negated with [[aranea boots]]. Players should use [[Protect from Missiles]] when Sarachnis shoots the web to block her next ranged attack, then quickly close to melee range and switch back to [[Protect from Melee]]. If done perfectly, players will take no damage from her attacks.

Tstanon is usually not considered a threat compared to K'ril, since most players already have [[Protect from Melee]] active while fighting the [[Zamorak]] bosses.

evidence.text: Like Ket-Zek, Jad's attacks can deal extremely high damage, and is even capable of killing lower-levelled players in one hit if not protected against. Jad's melee and ranged attacks have a max hit of 97, while the magic attack has a max hit of 95.

With a [[combat level]] of 702, TzTok-Jad has a max hit of 97 and can easily kill most players in one hit with any of its three attacks: a [[Melee]] attack with its bite (max hit of 97), a blast of [[Magic]] in the form of a fireball (max hit of 95), and a boulder falling from the ceiling as a [[Ranged]] attack (max hit of 97). To add to the challenge, players must fight through waves of monsters in the TzHaar Fight Cave in order to reach TzTok-Jad and must do so solo and without being able to restock on supplies from the previous waves.
